text.p: Tropical depression Fern is currently east of the Northern Marianas and is moving tracking east. Top winds have diminished to 30 mph. This system is dissipating as a significant cyclone. It is becoming less of a risk to shipping in the area.

Tropical cyclone Fergus is becoming extratropical as it crosses the North island of New Zealand. It is still causing winds up to 55 mph and will likely produce wind damage on the island. It also will generate heavy rain and cause flooding and possible mudslides as it moves across during the next 12 hours. Shipping in and around the area will also be at risk for another 6-12 hours.

Tropical cyclone Phil is mainly a risk to shipping as it stays off shore to the north of West Australia during the next 24-48 hours. However, coastal areas may have rough seas and possible beach errosion with the storm located just to the north. Top winds near the center of Phil have dropping to 75 mph. Further weakening may bring winds down to 65 mph in 24 hours and 55 mph in 48 hours.
